check.name: lens.design
check.reason: Melian shares none of this text, which the reviewing host's store and terminal hold

message.text: `retire` deletes a record-only changeset folder and leaves no mark (state-tree.ts:284 rules it "clean" when no cell is found; git-record-store.ts:292 removes it). `add` then accepts any later batch for that name as if the changeset had never existed, because it checks only `refuse` and `disposed` (git-record-store.ts:190-199). So a late add of records from before the retirement is treated as belonging to whatever the changeset is now. That might be nothing, or a reopened pull request's new life. Nothing tells the two apart.

evidence.snippet:
- `list` is fresh: it returns every record whose `add` returned before the call. A store that can only answer from a stale copy fails the call, and is no record store. The first draft let `list` be stale, and each rule built to survive that, a cell naming the rounds, a watermark for publication, was a new thing to forge.
- `readCell` is fresh: it returns the last value a `writeCell` stored.
- `writeCell` succeeds only when the cell's version is still `expectedVersion`. A version is opaque and changes on every successful write, never a hash of the value, and a writer that dies leaves nothing that blocks the next. The conformance suite holds the case of a value that went away and came back.
- `dispose` first writes a disposal mark to the cell, and `add` refuses a changeset whose cell holds one. Disposal is permanent: the port has no way to recreate a changeset, since one would need an incarnation every record and writer carries.

- **Standing is computed from the rounds.** A round of a revision stands when no round that counts names it as replaced. Nothing else says which round is current, so there is no pointer for a writer to roll back. Where a key is pinned, only a round that key signed counts, so only the trusted host's round can replace the trusted host's.
- **The gate takes the worst standing round.** Two rounds that stand together, because two hosts reviewed at once, gate by the worse, and not reviewed is worse than blocking.
- When the branch cannot be reached, a review works locally and adds its records later. `melian publish` and the gate refuse without the store.

That has one limit. A retired folder leaves no mark, so nothing refuses a stale host that relays the changeset's ordinary records after the retirement, such as a re-run of an old round's records job. It writes the folder again with those records, and they stay on the tip until the next run retires them. If the pull request has reopened in the meantime, they join its new records. Ordinary records carry no lease, so this touches no publication slot.

He agreed on 2026-11-22, in the coordinator's session, to two more ([comment](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/639#issuecomment-7071348428)). A retirement keeps any changeset folder that is disposed or holds a cell, and reports it as kept; rule 3 of the shared record decision stands as written. He also agreed to the warning's wording above.

explanation.what: `retire` deletes a record-only changeset folder and leaves no mark (state-tree.ts:284 rules it "clean" when no cell is found; git-record-store.ts:292 removes it). `add` then accepts any later batch for that name as if the changeset had never existed, because it checks only `refuse` and `disposed` (git-record-store.ts:190-199). So a late add of records from before the retirement is treated as belonging to whatever the changeset is now. That might be nothing, or a reopened pull request's new life. Nothing tells the two apart.
explanation.whatToDo: Before a retirement may let `add` start a changeset afresh, give the store a way to tell a pre-retirement record from a post-retirement one. Options: an incarnation carried by records and writers, as rule 3 requires; or a small retirement marker that refuses relays of records whose revision or round predates it. Otherwise, amend rule 3 explicitly and state which rounds may revive. Do not claim rule 3 stands while the change recreates changesets.
explanation.whyHere: Rule 3 of the active shared record decision says the port has no way to recreate a changeset, "since one would need an incarnation every record and writer carries". It also says `list` returns every record whose `add` returned before the call. The head decision says rule 3 "stands as written" and avoids recreating only cell-holding folders. That keeps the wording of rule 3 but breaks its reason. A record-only changeset is now recreated with no incarnation, and the head decision itself says stale records then "join its new records". Rule 4 decides which round stands only from which rounds are in the set. So bringing back a subset of an old incarnation can revive a round that a later round had replaced. The head decision amends rule 13 only, not rule 3.

properties.failureScenario:
1. Pull request #N's changeset `pull-x` holds round R1 for head H, which passed. It also holds round R2 for the same head H, which names R1 as replaced and blocks. R2 stands, so the gate fails.
2. The pull request is closed without merging. Thirty days later the scheduled job calls `retire(new Map([["pull-x", oid]]))`. The folder holds records only, so `judgeFolder` returns "clean" and `withoutFolders` removes it whole, with no mark.
3. A host that ran R1 adds R1's batch late. The base design allows this: "a review works locally and adds its records later", and the head decision's own example is a re-run of an old round's records job. `add` finds no folder and no disposal mark, so it writes R1's records back. R2 is not written back.
4. The pull request is reopened at head H. R1's reviewed base is an ancestor of `main`, and no round that counts names R1 as replaced. So R1 stands alone and `melian gate` passes the merge group on a revision whose last review blocked.

Without the retirement, R2 would still stand and block. A milder case: an old blocking round revives without the dismissal that had cleared it, and the reopened pull request reads blocked until it is dismissed again. In every case `list("pull-x")` before the late add returns none of the records whose `add` had returned, against rule 3's freshness promise.
